main_body: Rectangular farm plot (wheat, grass tufts, cabbages, seedlings on tilled soil) enclosed by a wooden post-and-rail fence. The posts and rails are the frame; the field fills the interior.
top_band: Posts: a light-brown cap with a dot, about 3-4 rows (rows 0-3), is the only part that reads as a top. The rails have a light brown upper strip (rows ~4-7) that is flush with the face rather than a separate top surface. The side rails are plain vertical strips with no top band.
evidence: Reading one column through a rail, I see a light strip, a dark gap, then a second lighter rail, all drawn face-on. The posts are flat vertical bars with a tiny cap. The rails and the base show no foreshortened horizontal top faces. The side rails are flat strips, and the south fence has no visible top or base surfaces. The interior field is drawn as a flat top-down plan. The frame is therefore a front elevation with small caps, not a 3/4 construction. Strict reading: fail.

style.evidence: The fence wood has about 4-5 brown steps, with a dark brown outline that leans toward the wood rather than neutral black. The wheat is a checker of yellow and ochre dots. The cabbages are shaded in 4 greens with highlights, and the soil and grass tufts carry grain. I see no large flat fills, and tile density is comparable to or higher than the reference. It would sit acceptably next to the stall and well references.
